index ed039b8..02456db 100644
--- a/gunicorn.conf.py
+++ b/gunicorn.conf.py
@@ -2,13 +2,6 @@
 # multi-worker deployment exposes one aggregated /metrics endpoint.
 from prometheus_flask_exporter.multiprocess import GunicornPrometheusMetrics
 
-# Threaded workers: each of gunicorn's -w processes now accepts up to
-# `threads` requests concurrently instead of one at a time. Bumped as part of
-# the same tuning pass that reduced the DB pool footprint below, to squeeze
-# more throughput out of fewer connections.
-worker_class = "gthread"
-threads = 8
-
 
 def when_ready(server):
     # Serve aggregated metrics from the gunicorn master on a dedicated port,
diff --git a/postmortem.md b/postmortem.md
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..972cd9c
--- /dev/null
+++ b/postmortem.md
@@ -0,0 +1 @@
+Root cause: Commit 6684fb1 caused DB connection starvation by limiting the SQLAlchemy pool size to 1 while increasing gunicorn worker threads to 8. This caused concurrent requests to block waiting for DB connections, spiking p99 latency.\nEvidence used: Alert manager notification, Prometheus queries showing p99 latency around 1.0s to 1.7s, and git log inspection pointing to the recent tuning change.\nWhat I changed: Reverted commit 6684fb1 to restore single-threaded gunicorn workers and default SQLAlchemy connection pool sizes, eliminating the connection contention.
